title: POC scoping - open model shortlist (Aurelia Therapeutics)
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet and cost model
Run 1-week latency + cost pilot against 3 open models (Llama3-13B, Mistral Large, Falcon 40B)
Customer to share 100 representative prompts and 2k anonymized records for evaluation
Schedule on-prem/private deployment feasibility call (if POC looks good) - target week of 2026-09-28
action_items: Maya Chen: send pricing and benchmark template by 2026-09-17
Ravi Patel: draft pilot infra architecture (Dedicated vs Hosted comparison) by 2026-09-22
Dr. Elena Ramirez: provide representative prompt set and small anonymized dataset by 2026-09-18
Priya Sharma: confirm expected qps and concurrency patterns (peak/avg) by 2026-09-17
summary: Discovery-focused POC scoping to choose an open-model shortlist for a medical-text extraction and triage POC. Primary success criteria: extraction accuracy on clinical notes, response latency < 400ms p50, cost target to be defined. Spanish and Portuguese support and hallucination risk mitigation are key. Redwood proposed three candidate models and a 1-week benchmark plan. Next steps: share benchmark template, customer to share prompts and sample data, run hosted benchmarks, then consider Dedicated/private pilot if promising.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I see Dr. Elena, Mark, Priya — thanks for joining. Quick agenda: align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist open models, and agree on benchmarks and timeline.
[00:18] Dr. Elena Ramirez: Hi Maya, hi Ravi, thanks. We're excited; main goal is to validate model quality on clinical extraction and triage — mostly unstructured clinician notes, some intake forms. Spanish + Portuguese are important too.
[00:32] Mark Voss: From infra side, we care about latency for live triage, and also cost because we'll deploy at scale across clinics.
[00:40] Ravi Patel: Great. Can you quantify expected request profile? qps, tokens per request?
[00:46] Priya Sharma: Typical request is a note ~400-800 tokens, often we ask for structured JSON output with extracted fields plus confidence. Peak qps expected around 15-20 qps, average 4-6, concurrency up to ~50 during rush windows.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: OK that's useful. For latency SLO, what are you targeting? p50 vs p95?
[01:10] Dr. Elena Ramirez: We want p50 under 400ms for token generation, p95 ideally under 900ms, but we can be flexible if we can get accuracy gains.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Good constraints. Success criteria recap: extraction F1 on labeled dev set (you'll share) > 0.88 for key fields, latency p50 < 400ms, cost target TBD but ballpark we discussed internally. Any regulatory needs?
[01:35] Mark Voss: We need audit logs, KMS integration, and likely SOC 2 attestation. Private deployment may be required for production later.
[01:44] Maya Chen: Redwood supports private (VPC/on‑prem) and Dedicated. We'll include compliance docs.
[01:49] Carlos Mendes: Quick question on hallucination — medical domain is sensitive. How do you recommend measuring hallucination risk in the POC?
[01:55] Ravi Patel: We typically include a hallucination test set: prompts where correct answer is empty or 'no extraction' and measure false positives, plus a factuality checklist. We can instrument confidence scores and calibrate thresholds.
[02:06] Dr. Elena Ramirez: Good. For models, we discussed open models — which ones do you recommend for multilingual medical text?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: From our experience and model profiles, we usually shortlist three for this workload: Llama 3 13B (base and quantized), Mistral Large (7B/Chat variants), and Falcon 40B. Tradeoffs: Llama 3 13B tends to be strong general reasoning and performs well when fine‑tuned/adapter'd; Mistral has great token efficiency and cost profile; Falcon 40B has good multilingual breadth but is heavier and more expensive to run.
[02:41] Maya Chen: I'll add a note — mixed results reported on Spanish specialized medical terminology; we'll need to validate with your sample prompts. Also consider instruction‑tuned vs base model variants.
[02:52] Priya Sharma: Are there quantized variants we should test? Our infra prefers 8‑bit or q4 to save memory.
[02:57] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can run q8 and q4 benchmarks. For Falcon 40B we recommend q4f16 profiles on GPUs for throughput. For Llama 3 13B q8_0 or q4a variants often hit a sweet spot, but there can be accuracy regressions — we'll measure that.
[03:15] Dr. Elena Ramirez: How do you propose running the benchmark technically? Hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated vs Private?
[03:22] Maya Chen: For POC, we recommend starting hosted to validate model quality quickly (faster setup), then run a Dedicated pilot to measure realistic latency/cost if hosted looks promising. If data sensitivity pushes you, we can run the benchmark on a private dedicated node (we can provide a private trial).
[03:36] Mark Voss: If we run hosted, can we get raw logs / token‑level cost breakdown?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes, the Console provides token‑level cost, per‑route latency, traces, and you can request extended logs. For strict security we'll switch to VPC/private where logs stay in your environment.
[03:50] Carlos Mendes: Any red flags around inference accuracy when models are quantized?
[03:55] Ravi Patel: Some drop, especially on generative tasks requiring precise phrasing. Extraction tasks often tolerate quantization better, but we'll measure F1 on your tests. We'll include quality vs cost curves in the benchmark deliverable.
[04:08] Dr. Elena Ramirez: For multilingual, is there a specific model that historically handles Spanish/Portuguese better out of those three?
[04:14] Ravi Patel: Anecdotally, Falcon 40B has broader multilingual pretraining and sometimes performs better zero‑shot on non‑English, but Llama 3 with fine‑tuning/instruction tuning can catch up. Mistral tends to be more English‑optimized, though you might see decent results on common languages. We'll surface per‑language metrics.
[04:34] Priya Sharma: What's the expected GPU footprint for the pilot? We're estimating 8‑16GB per model instance if quantized, but need concrete numbers to reserve capacity.
[04:44] Ravi Patel: For q4_0 Llama 3 13B you can get away with 24GB A10‑type GPU or even 16GB with packing; Falcon 40B will generally need 80GB‑class (A100 80GB or multi‑card sharding) unless aggressively quantized which can impact quality. Mistral Large is in the 48GB class depending on token lengths and batching. We'll include config recommendations in the infra doc.
[05:05] Dr. Elena Ramirez: Good. For benchmarks, can we quantify the test set size and duration?
[05:10] Maya Chen: We suggest a week‑long run with 5k‑10k representative prompts for quality metrics and a handful of synthetic load tests for throughput: e.g., steady 10 qps and spike tests to 50 qps. Also a 1k prompt per‑language subset for Spanish and Portuguese to measure language‑specific quality.
[05:27] Mark Voss: Cost modeling — can you show cost per 1k requests at different model choices?
[05:32] Maya Chen: Yes, the benchmark spreadsheet will include cost per 1k requests and cost per 1M tokens for each model + quantization variant + deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
[05:43] Priya Sharma: Timeline — if we start next week, how long until we have results?
[05:47] Ravi Patel: If we get the prompt set and sample data this week, we can spin up bench infra and return initial quality reports in ~7 business days. Dedicated pilot numbers (realistic latency/cost) may take another week.
[05:59] Dr. Elena Ramirez: That works. One more thing: evaluation metrics — besides F1, we want false positive rate for hallucinations and slot‑level accuracy.
[06:08] Maya Chen: We'll add those metrics to the spreadsheet. Also will include example prompts and a template for annotated labels.
[06:15] Carlos Mendes: Any compliance checklist you can share? Some of our legal folks asked for encryption in transit and at rest and KMS integration.
[06:23] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC 2, ISO and KMS integration docs to the follow‑up. For private deployments we support bring‑your‑own‑KMS and HSM options.
[06:33] Mark Voss: If the POC looks good, what's typical pilot -> production ramp? Time and blockers?
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: From CSM perspective, pilot to prod varies but often 8‑12 weeks depending on security review and infra readiness. Blockers: data residency, KPI validation, and procurement.
[06:49] Dr. Elena Ramirez: OK. For the shortlist, can you summarize recommended configuration for each model we will test?
[06:55] Ravi Patel: Sure: Llama 3 13B - q8_0 baseline, instruction‑tuned variant; Mistral Large - q8/q4 tradeoff, use chat/instruct tuned if available; Falcon 40B - test both 40B base and an optimized 40B chat variant, prefer q4f16 for throughput. We'll include kernel/runtime hints — e.g., batch sizes, KV cache strategies.
[07:13] Priya Sharma: For your automated batching and KV cache, will Redwood handle prefix caching for repeated patient notes?
[07:19] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood has prefix/KV caching and smart batching. There's also caching policies you can tune per‑route. Occasionally the transcriptions say 'KV cash' in our logs but it's KV cache, sorry for that.
[07:31] Dr. Elena Ramirez: Sounds good. Can we get an example of the deliverable? A short sample report?
[07:36] Ravi Patel: We'll include a sample benchmark report and the spreadsheet. It will have per‑model tables: accuracy, hallucination FP rate, latency p50/p95, throughput, cost estimates, and recommended deployment profile.
[07:47] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: Redwood sends benchmark template + security docs by Thursday 2026-09-17; Aurelia shares prompt set + sample data by 2026-09-18; Redwood runs hosted benchmarks across the three shortlisted models and returns initial results by 2026-09-25; follow-up call to review results the week of 2026-09-28.
[08:08] Mark Voss: Perfect. Any blockers on our side? Priya: will coordinate data extraction and anonymization.
[08:14] Priya Sharma: Yep, we'll anonymize and drop PHI fields, share the dataset subset.
[08:18] Dr. Elena Ramirez: Thanks, looking forward. Also note we may want to include a clinical SME during evaluation to validate edge cases.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Great idea — include them in the review. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[08:31] (call ends)
